Every pair of nodes is joined, giving 3, 6, and 15 edges." width="100%"} Creates `n` nodes where every node is connected to every other node. How many edges that takes depends on the graph's directedness: - undirected graphs get one edge per pair: `n(n - 1) / 2` edges - directed graphs get an edge in each direction for every pair: `n(n - 1)` edges With `keep_loops=True`, each node also gets a self-loop, adding `n` more edges. The new nodes are appended to the graph without touching or connecting to existing nodes. Complete graphs are the densest possible simple graphs, which makes them useful for: - modeling groups in which everyone interacts with everyone (a team, a committee) - creating dense cliques to plant inside sparser graphs, e.g. to test community or clique detection - checking edge cases, since every node has the maximum possible degree of `n - 1` The edge count grows quadratically, so large values of `n=` produce very many edges (`n=1000` already gives about half a million in an undirected graph). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the clique. Must be at least `1`; smaller values raise a `ValueError`. With `n=1` a single node is added with no edges (unless `keep_loops=` is `True`). [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string (so `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in an empty graph); a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge, including any self-loops. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [keep_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, also add a self-loop on every new node, adding `n` edges and making the graph non-simple. Default is `False` (no self-loops). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A complete graph connects every pair of nodes, so `n` nodes produce `n(n-1)/2` edges -- here, `4 * 3 / 2 = 6`: ::: {#ccec2fc6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (4, 6) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph each pair is joined in both directions, so the same `n=3` clique has `6` edges instead of `3`: ::: {#e9e42ad3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_full_graph(n=3) directed.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1->2', '1->3', '2->1', '2->3', '3->1', '3->2'] ``` ::: ::: `keep_loops=True` adds a self-loop on every node -- the `"1--1"`, `"2--2"`, and `"3--3"` entries below -- so the graph is no longer simple: ::: {#ff3bf414 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} looped = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=3, keep_loops=True) looped.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True), looped.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (['1--1', '1--2', '1--3', '2--2', '2--3', '3--3'], False) ``` ::: :::
